# Kettle River Business Intelligence (Kettle River BI, KRBI)

> Fractional BI analyst and project manager for manufacturers. Kettle River BI aligns Finance, Operations, and IT around one set of numbers, then builds the dashboards and accountability structures that turn those numbers into action. Based in Kettle Falls, WA; serving manufacturers across the United States.

Key facts:
- Founder & Principal: Mitch Cauthron (contact: info@kettleriverbi.com). Accounting and business administration degree (2010). 15+ years across healthcare, food manufacturing, and heavy civil construction. At Tillamook: staff accountant, then financial analyst, then cost analyst on the ice cream product line; rebuilt budget prep (Jet Reports templates + VBA consolidation into Dynamics NAV with versioned budgets), cutting the cycle from weeks to days. At Oregon Ice Cream: plant controller; implemented Power BI, built operations datasets (downtime, waste, efficiency, opex, capex), and replaced paper inventory counts with a tablet-based real-time counting program. Four years in heavy civil construction as finance and procurement manager, building a five-analyst internal BI team. Every KRBI engagement is scoped, led, and delivered by the principal.
- Primary industry focus: food manufacturing; also construction and broader manufacturing
- Positioning: enterprise-level business intelligence at a fraction of the cost of a full-time analyst
- Primary tools: Power BI, SQL, Excel/VBA, Microsoft Power Platform
- Typical engagement: a 2-week assessment, then a 30 to 45 day foundation build, then an ongoing monthly retainer. Measurable progress within the first 90 days.
- Pricing (fixed-price, published; KRBI does not bill hourly): Data Health Assessment $5,000 fixed for 2 weeks, credited in full against a build signed within 90 days. Foundation Build $35,000-$55,000 fixed for 30 to 45 days, priced from the assessment findings rather than estimated in advance. Managed Intelligence $3,500 per month ongoing ($42,000 a year), covering data quality monitoring, maintenance, and a monthly operations review call. A governance audit of an existing Power BI estate runs as the assessment: same $5,000, findings report and remediation roadmap in 10 business days.
- Payment terms: 40% on signature, 40% at design sign-off, 20% at reconciled delivery. The final 20% is held until Finance and Operations pull the same report and get the same number.
- Works with any ERP or none: QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, spreadsheets, operational databases

What makes KRBI different: most BI consultants start by asking what reports you want. KRBI starts by asking what decisions you need to make and who owns the outcome, then gets Finance, Operations, and IT to agree on metric definitions before building anything.

Track record (published testimonials; spans KRBI client engagements and Mitch's prior in-house roles):
- Smith Brothers (KRBI client; COO, Sebastian Pastore): replaced hundreds of siloed Excel tools with shared BI reporting; normalized 37.7% YoY loss and waste reduction, measured like for like.
- Oregon Ice Cream (former employer, current KRBI client; VP of Operations, Charles Nutter): Mitch served as plant controller, implemented Power BI dashboarding and KPI tracking, and continues to manage their Power BI environment as a client engagement today.
- Tillamook Cheese (prior in-house role; CFO, Linda Pearce): as cost analyst, Mitch rebuilt budget prep, cutting the cycle from weeks to days with versioned budgets and variance reporting.
- Goodfellow Bros Inc. (prior in-house role; Director of Finance, Travis Hendrick): a Power BI initiative had stalled for six months; Mitch taught himself the ERP and database and shipped the first successful deployment within a month, then built a five-analyst internal BI team.
- A Director of Finance (Kent Walker): automated budget upload and reporting, saving the budget team weeks of work.

## Pages

- [Home](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/): The problem KRBI solves. Finance, Operations, and Sales report different numbers for the same thing; nobody acts on a number they don't understand. Approach: align on definitions, quantify against source systems, assign ownership.
- [Data Governance](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/governance): Three-part governance framework: alignment (departments define metrics together), quantification (trace each metric to a single source of truth), ownership (a named person reviews each metric on a cadence).
- [KPI Dashboards](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/dashboards): Power BI reporting connected to accountability. Start with the decision, work backward to the metric, give every metric an owner.
- [Insights & Alignment](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/insights): Surfacing the disagreements hiding in manufacturing data and turning them into shared definitions leadership teams act on.
- [Pricing](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/pricing): What fractional BI costs at Kettle River BI. The three-stage engagement ladder with published fixed prices, the pricing rules (no hourly rate, three options in every proposal, bounded reconciliation scope, client-delay re-baseline, written answer to who maintains the system if KRBI disappears), the 40/40/20 payment schedule, and a pricing FAQ.
- [Case Study](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/case-study): Smith Brothers, a packaged food manufacturer. Finance, Operations, Sales, and Warehouse each measured loss and waste from a different source, and the views did not reconcile. KRBI aligned all departments on one definition, redesigned inventory adjustment reason codes, and implemented cycle counting in NetSuite. Result: a normalized 37.7% year-over-year reduction in loss and waste, with every loss account improving. The figure excludes commodity price movement (milk variance) and a one-time acquisition inventory write-off, and compares the same months and the same continuing locations in both years. KRBI publishes the normalized figure rather than the raw 60.6% change.
